input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: a Content-Type parameter without an equals sign is stored with the value True instead of being skipped
- failure path: the header `text/html; charset` yields params['charset'] == True; get_encoding_from_headers (shown below the change) returns params['charset'].strip(...) which raises AttributeError on a bool, so reading response.text for such a response fails instead of falling back to ISO-8859-1

Reviewer finding
- description: A parameter token without '=' is now stored with the boolean value True. get_encoding_from_headers then calls .strip() on that value when the key is 'charset', which raises AttributeError.
- rationale: Trigger: a response header such as 'Content-Type: text/html; charset' (bare charset token, no '='). The new code sets params['charset'] = True, so get_encoding_from_headers reaches params['charset'].strip(...) on a bool. Mechanism: the value is no longer a string, but the caller assumes it is. Impact: accessing response.encoding, or any code path that reads it, raises an exception on a malformed header that previously returned a fallback encoding.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. A bare 'charset' parameter is stored as True, and get_encoding_from_headers then calls .strip() on that bool and raises AttributeError instead of falling back to the default encoding.
